full_judgment:
2. The plaintiff-Respondent Nos. 1-10 filed the suit stating, inter alia, that the land in suit measuring 4.08 acres of C.S. Khatian No. 876 corresponding to S.A. Khatian No. 1 of Monza Machine belonged to Dhirendra Nath Roy, Zamindar of Nandi Zamindari Estate, that the Zamindar orally settled the land to the plaintiffs on 20th Poush, 1354 B.S. and since then plaintiffs are in possession of the land in suit. It was also the case of the plaintiffs that the defendant Nos. 2 and 3 claimed title in the land in suit in the month of Bhadra, 1383 B.S. disclosing that they have taken settlement from the Government and then on enquiry plaintiffs came to know from the local thesis office that the land in suit has been incorrectly recorded in S.A. Khatian in the name of the Government and the said wrong recording having had clouted plaintiffs' title they were constrained to file the suit seeking declaration of title and confirmation of possession. 

 3. The suit was contested by the defendant No. 1, Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh by filling written statement denying the material averments made in the plaint and stating, inter alia, that the land in suit was retainable khas land of the Zamindar and  that the land in suit with other non-retainable lands of the Zamindar vested with the Government as per provision of section 20(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and that during S.A. survey operation the land was correctly recorded in the khas khatian No. 1 in the name of the Government and that the Government has given permanent lease to different persons on different dates and the lessees are in possession of the land in suit. It was also the case of the contesting defendant that the plaintiffs by creating forged and ante-dated documents want to grab the land in suit. 

 6. The contesting defendant went on appeal. The appellate Court noticed that the contesting defendant in support of its claim that the land in suit was the non-retainable land of  the Zamindar and the same was acquired as per provision of section 20 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act did not file any paper relating to preparation of compensation assessment roll and compensation, if any, paid to the ex-zamindar or that compensation was assessed but the zamindar did not withdraw the same in spite of payment and thereupon  observed "In the absence of the same it is very much hard to believe the defence contention that the suit lands have been duly acquired by the Government under section 20(2) of the S.A. non & T. Act, as non-retainable khas properties of the admitted ex-zamihdar". The appellate Court also observed that although contesting defendant claimed that the land in suit has been leased out by the Government and the same is possessed by the lessees on the basis of the registered kabuliyat which were produced before the trial Court and were marked as Exts. but later on the same were taken back and were not produced before the appellate Court and as such adverse presumption in the light of the provision of section 114(h) of the Evidence Act can very much be drawn as to the genuineness of the said documents and the lessees, as claimed by the defendant, are not witness in the case in support of the claim of the defendant that the lessees are in possession of the land in suit. In the background of the aforesaid observations the appellate Court held the Government has failed to prove that the suit lands were nonreturnable khas lands of the ex-zamindar of Narail and Government acquired the same under section 20(2)of the S.A. & T. Act and since then it has been possessing through its lessees". 

 8. The P. W. 1, one of the plaintiffs, while deposing in support of plaintiffs' claim of taking settlement of the land in suit stated that at the time of taking pattan Mongal Gazi, Syed Ali, Shahadat, Obaidullah and Hussain Sardar were present but the plaintiffs for the purpose of corroborating P.W. 1 so far his evidence relating to pattan did not examine none of the persons claimed to have been present at the time of pattan but examined P.Ws. 2 and 3 who were not the persons, as mentioned by P.W.1, present at the time of paten. It may also be mentioned no explanation was offered by the plaintiffs for non-examination of the persons who, as being ready for claimed by the P.W.1, were present at the time of pattan. The appellate Court in the afore state of the matter placed no reliance on the P.Ws. 2 and 3 who were examined to corroborate the P.W. 1 as regard the matter of pattan. 

 9. It was the case of the plaintiffs that talk of the pattan took place with the Manager of the Zamindar. In that background the appellate Court observed that no material was brought on record to show that the Manager of the ex- zamindar was competent to settle the land and that no material was also brought on record, that at the time of talk of pattan Zamindar was present or consented to the pattan or received the salami. The appellate Court also noticed that dakhilas produced by the plaintiffs in support of their case of taking pattan of the land in suit do not bear the signature of the Manager who, as claimed by the plaintiffs settled the land, that the scribe of the plaintiffs settled the land, that the scribe of the dakhilas i.e. Naib of the ex-zamindar was not examined and for such non- examination no explanation was offered. On examination and scrutiny of the dakhilas the appellate Court arrived at the finding "The dakhilas Ext.1 series found to have been made old by artificial means and the close scrutiny of the same clearly indicates that the same were written in one sitting by an in-experienced hand  The Ext.1 series in no way inspire confidence about its age as shown thereto", and the claim of the P.Ws.2 and 3 of their being present at the time of pattan can not be accepted since P. W.1 has not stated about the presence of the said witnesses at the time of taking pattan; by the plaintiffs and that the said witnesses "failed to prove the particulars of the dakhilas Ext. 1 series". In the afore state of the matter the appellate Court arrived at the finding "I do not find any reason to believe that they (EWs.2-3) were present at the time of granting the dakhilas Ext. 1 series or their presence at the time of alleged Inman- or that the same i.e. pattan had actually taken place. 

 12. The High Court Division while making the Rule absolute placed reliance on some of the observations as to the case of the respective parties made by the appellate Court and in the background of the said observations, as stated hereinbefore, the High Court Division held that the appellate Court was in error in reversing the judgment of the trial Court. As to the genuineness of the Ext.1 series the High Court Division has observed, The trial Court found the rent receipts, Ext. 1 series, to be genuine. I myself also examined the rent receipts which is in a printed form and same appears to be genuine". On the point as regard the question of possession of the parties in the land in suit the High Court Division has observed that the Government failed to prove their possession by producing their lessees and thereupon observed "Thus I find that the trial Court has rightly decreed the suit". 

 16. The appellate Court while reversing the judgment of the trial Court has rejected the evidence of P.Ws.2 and 3 who examined from the side of the plaintiffs to corroborate the P.W.1 as regard the case of taking pattan of the land from the Ex-zamindar since the said P.Ws. were not the persons whom the P.W.1 stated were present at the time of pattan. The High Court Division while making the Rule absolute did not reverse the reasoning and the finding given by the appellate Court in rejecting the evidence of P.Ws. 2 and 3. 

 18. In the afore state of the matter we are of the view that the High Court Division was in serious error in disturbing the finding of fact arrived at by the appellate Court when the said Division did not hold that the finding and decision made by the appellate Court was vitiated by non-consideration of the evidence or misreading of evidence or that the appellate Court left the vital evidence out of consideration for no valid reason while making its decision on the question of taking pattan of the land in suit by the plaintiffs and the nature and character of the Ext.1 series as well as regarding possession of the plaintiffs.
